motivation: After rejecting the original RCB candidate, run one additional predeclared trial. Natural free generation rarely starts with the neutral label. Compare a constrained verdict alone with a discriminatively calibrated output layer under that same constraint. Use a fresh independent external benchmark once.
training: Only the same 339 MIT-licensed RCB training items and 48 RCB development items. Use frozen final-layer vectors, a class-balanced regularized multiclass logistic objective and a linear bias feature. Select regularization and feature rank exclusively on RCB development macro-F1. The first and second candidates are distinct. No XNLI text or labels may enter fitting or model selection.
validation: 90 new balanced Russian XNLI test items, premise-disjoint and filtered outside the business head. Only local research evaluation uses XNLI (Conneau et al., CC BY-NC 4.0). Do not ship XNLI text. The old 83 RCB items are now explicitly a regression panel, not a new blind exam.
acceptance: Against the previous release, require at least five additional correct out of 90 and improved macro-F1 on the fresh XNLI exam. Also require a gain over grammar-only on that exam, at least five additional RCB answers over the original 32/83 and improved RCB macro-F1, no loss exceeding ten percentage points for any of the three 30-item XNLI classes, plus unchanged business and unrestricted generation controls. If any gate fails, keep 3.2.1 verification weights. Do not retune after either panel is seen.
budget: One unchanged local GPU, reuse the original training features, one candidate and one final evaluation. Stop new weight experiments after this trial.
rollback: Use the former VerifyClaim path and remove the new head. Preserve the user's personal adapter, base GGUF and the existing business head.
